title: What If You Enjoy the Sin You’re Trying to Quit?
paragraphs:
What If You Enjoy the Sin You’re Trying to Quit?
The secret battle nobody admits… and the grace nobody expects
You didn’t expect to like it this much.
That’s the part that scares you.
Because it’s not just that you keep falling… it’s that somewhere inside, there’s a part of you that doesn’t want to stop.
And you hate that part.
You pray, you cry, you promise God, “This is the last time,” but when the moment comes… your heart doesn’t run away. It leans in.
You don’t just sin.
You enjoy it.
And now you’re stuck in the most silent kind of guilt—the kind that whispers, “If I really loved God… why does this feel good?”
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected.
Because deep down, you’ve asked the question you were too afraid to say out loud:
“What if I don’t actually want to change?”
The apostle Paul asked something dangerously similar, and he didn’t hide it.
In Romans 7:15, he writes:
“For what I am doing, I do not understand; for what I want, this I do not practice, but what I hate, this I do.”
He goes further in verse 22–23:
“συνήδομαι γὰρ τῷ νόμῳ τοῦ Θεοῦ… βλέπω δὲ ἕτερον νόμον ἐν τοῖς μέλεσίν μου…”
“For I delight (συνήδομαι — I rejoice with) in the law of God in my inner being, but I see another law in my members…”
Did you catch that?
There are two desires inside one person.
One that loves God.
One that loves sin.
And they don’t take turns… they fight at the same time.
So if you feel like you’re living a double life inside your own chest… you’re not alone.
You’re human.
Even deeper, the Hebrew understanding of the heart—לֵב (lev)—was never just emotions. It was the seat of will, desire, intention.
Meaning… your “heart” can want God and want sin at the same time.
That tension doesn’t make you fake.
It reveals the war.
But here’s where most people get it wrong…
They think the problem is that sin feels good.
But Scripture never denies that.
Hebrews 11:25 calls it exactly what it is:
“ἀπόλαυσιν ἁμαρτίας” — the fleeting pleasure of sin.
Not imaginary pleasure.
Real pleasure.
Temporary.
Deceptive.
But real.
And that’s why it’s so powerful.
Sin doesn’t show up ugly.
It shows up desirable.
From the very beginning, Genesis 3:6 says:
“וַתֵּרֶא הָאִשָּׁה כִּי־טוֹב הָעֵץ לְמַאֲכָל…”
“And the woman saw that the tree was good for food…”
Sin was seen as good before it was known as deadly.
So if you’re waiting for sin to feel disgusting before you leave it… you will stay stuck longer than you think.
Because the trap isn’t just in the act.
It’s in the desire.
And desire doesn’t disappear just because you hate the consequences.
This is where Jesus goes deeper than behavior.
In Matthew 26:41, He says:
“τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα πρόθυμον, ἡ δὲ σὰρξ ἀσθενής.”
“The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
The word σὰρξ (sarx)—flesh—is not just your body.
It’s the part of you still wired toward rebellion.
The part that can enjoy what is destroying you.
So what if you enjoy the sin you’re trying to quit?
Then the battle is not fake.
It’s real.
And real battles require more than guilt.
They require surrender.
Because here’s the truth nobody told you clearly enough:
You don’t defeat sin by pretending it’s not enjoyable.
You defeat it by discovering something better.
Psalm 16:11 says in Hebrew:
“שֹׂבַע שְׂמָחוֹת אֶת־פָּנֶיךָ… נְעִמוֹת בִּימִינְךָ נֶצַח”
“In Your presence is fullness of joy… at Your right hand are pleasures forevermore.”
Not weaker pleasure.
Stronger.
Deeper.
Lasting.
Sin offers a spark.
God offers a fire that doesn’t burn out.
But here’s where it gets personal…
Because some of you aren’t struggling because you don’t know God.
You’re struggling because you haven’t stayed close long enough to taste Him fully.
So sin still feels louder.
More immediate.
More satisfying.
And you’re trying to fight it with willpower instead of intimacy.
That’s why you keep going back.
Because whatever you feed grows.
And whatever you starve weakens.
So if you feed your flesh all week and only visit God occasionally… don’t be surprised which voice feels stronger.
This isn’t condemnation.
This is clarity.
Because grace doesn’t just forgive you.
It teaches you.
Titus 2:11–12 says:
“ἡ γὰρ χάρις τοῦ Θεοῦ… παιδεύουσα ἡμᾶς…”
“For the grace of God… is training us…”
Grace is not permission to stay stuck.
It’s power to walk free.
But freedom doesn’t always feel immediate.
Sometimes it feels like war.
Sometimes it feels like loss.
Sometimes it feels like letting go of something you still crave.
And that’s the part nobody posts about.
But that’s also the place where transformation begins.
So if you’re in that place right now…
Where you hate your sin but still crave it…
Where you love God but still fall…
Where you’re tired of pretending you’re okay…
Because healing starts where honesty begins.
And listen carefully…
Your struggle does not disqualify you.
Your surrender is what God is looking for.
Not perfection.
Not performance.
Surrender.
Because the same Paul who cried out in Romans 7 didn’t end there.
He said in Romans 7:24–25:
“ταλαίπωρος ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπος… τίς με ῥύσεται…; χάρις δὲ τῷ Θεῷ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ…”
“O wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me…? Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ…”
The answer was never “try harder.”
The answer was always Jesus.
And Jesus doesn’t just forgive your sin.
He breaks its power.
But you have to come out of hiding.
You’re not just supporting content… you’re helping reach souls who are drowning in silence right now.
Because this isn’t just content.
This is a call.
And the part of you that still enjoys sin…
Is not the end of your story.
It’s the battlefield where Jesus is about to rewrite everything.
